summary:
SAR Sentinel India is an environmental monitoring platform that uses satellite remote sensing, Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and GIS to study rivers and environmental changes. Developed using NASA-ISRO NISAR data and Sentinel-2 satellite imagery, the platform currently focuses on the Kaveri and Tungabhadra river basins.

We developed a web-based dashboard that integrates satellite observations, processes radar and optical imagery, and displays geographical information through interactive maps and analysis tools. It includes preliminary water detection, vegetation-index analysis and environmental monitoring features.

Our project addresses the challenge of making complex satellite data easier to access, understand and explore. By bringing different satellite observations together in one platform, SAR Sentinel India aims to support environmental awareness, river monitoring and future research. It demonstrates how open Earth observation data can be transformed into practical tools for understanding changes happening on our planet.
details:
What does the project do and how does it work?

SAR Sentinel India is a web-based environmental monitoring platform that uses satellite remote sensing and GIS to study rivers and changes in the surrounding environment. It currently focuses on the Kaveri and Tungabhadra river basins.

The platform integrates NASA-ISRO NISAR radar data and ESA Sentinel-2 optical imagery. It processes satellite observations to support preliminary water detection and vegetation analysis using indices such as NDVI, EVI and NDMI. The results are presented through interactive maps and monitoring dashboards.

What are its benefits and intended impact?

The project makes satellite observations easier to access, explore and understand. It aims to support river monitoring, environmental awareness, vegetation studies and future research. Our long-term goal is to expand the platform to cover more Indian rivers and environmental applications.

What tools and technologies did you use?

  • Programming: Python and JavaScript
  • Backend: FastAPI and SQLite
  • Frontend: React and Vite
  • GIS and image processing: Rasterio, GDAL, GeoPandas and Shapely
  • Mapping: Leaflet and OpenStreetMap
  • Satellite data: NASA-ISRO NISAR and ESA Sentinel-2
  • Development and deployment: Git, GitHub, VS Code, Playwright, Vercel and Render

What makes the project creative?

Our project combines radar and optical satellite observations in a single environmental monitoring platform. Instead of presenting satellite data as complicated technical files, we transform available observations into maps, visualizations and understandable summaries.

What factors did the team consider?

We considered satellite data availability, geographical coverage, processing requirements, accuracy, accessibility, scalability and scientific reliability. We also considered the limitations of preliminary satellite analysis and clearly distinguished between candidate observations and scientifically validated results.
